newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures weaken with tech sector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures weaken with tech sector.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures opened slightly lower, mirroring weakness in the technology sector.
Microsoft Corp was down 4 to 145-1/2 early in an earnings-related setback. The company late Thursday released quarterly results that were in line with analysts' forecasts according to First Call.
Microsoft Corp said its fiscal fourth quarter earnings were 80 cents per share, 1 cent above the forecast and up from 43 cents in the year-ago quarter.
However, investors had pushed up Microsoft shares this week on the theory that the company's earnings would exceed expectations as they have often in previous quarter, traders said.
Microsoft shares were last down 7 3/8 points at 142 1/8, and CME Nasdaq 100 index futures were off 27.50 at 1080.00.
After a slightly lower opening, S&P 500 index futures' declines quickly snowballed, and the September contract plunged the 15.0-point trading limit.
Traders said Sept hit sell-stops at 932.00 and 930.00, then it was a straight drop to 925.00.
"We hit a vacuum there on the downside," said one S&P futures broker.
Traders said the Nasdaq Composite index continued to dictate direction in S&Ps.
"Everybody's watching the tech stocks. They are having a roller-coaster ride in the Nasdaq, and that is spilling over into the S&Ps," said a second S&P broker.

September S&Ps traded above the 15-point lower limit, then resumed their downward path when the next limit of 30 points went into effect. However, losses stalled at 917.50, a roughly 20-point decline.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was last trading down about 110 points at 7910, and September Treasury bond futures were down 1/2 point at 114-05/32.
The selloff pushed Sept S&Ps to their lowest level in more than a week. Support lies at 906.50, the July 9 low.

S&P 500 futures were down 14.75 points at 923.25, Nasdaq 100s down 25.50 at 1082.00, Russell 2000s down 5.25 at 408.00, Nikkei 225 index futures down 275.0 at 20,230.0 and Midcap 400s down 2.60 to 304.75.
